name: choice-poll

frames.best_why: Frame 6 shows the finished results: full bars, percentages, the voted tick and the footer, with no cursor.

tagline: Pick one answer, then the rows fill to show the vote split.
summary: A one-question poll: a heading and description over four radio rows. Choosing one locks the vote and turns every row into a bar with its share, a percentage and the total count.
appearance: A dark card holds a bold question, a small muted sentence, and four stacked rounded rows with thin outlines. Each row starts with a circular marker and a label; after voting a soft fill grows from the left of each row and a percentage sits at the right.
behaviour: Hovering lights a row's border and background. Clicking one fills its marker with a tick, disables the rows, and reveals results: each bar grows to its share, percentages count up, and a footer shows the total votes and a "You voted" mark.
demo_content: Question "What is your favorite frontend framework?" with React, Vue, Angular and Svelte, showing 650 votes.
search_phrases: vote for one option in a poll
choose one answer then see totals
use_when: You want a one-question vote on the page and to show the split once the visitor answers.
avoid_when: There is no backend: votes and hasVoted must be wired up yourself or the poll shows nothing real.
customise: Root takes value, multiple, disabled, showResults, votes and hasVoted; the heading, description and option rows are passed as child components. Styling is class-based.
weight_why: Four rows of DOM with short CSS transitions and a one-shot frame counter per bar.

a11y.note: Arrow keys, Home and End move between options, but the listbox has no accessible name and percentage changes are not announced.

issues: Before voting the right side of each row is empty, leaving an awkward gap.
After voting every row is disabled, so a visitor cannot change their answer.
polish_why: Clear rows and smooth result bars; the unused right side before voting is a small gap.
title: Choice Poll
